content.text:
The nested-link bug is fixed: a link whose text contains another link is no longer produced, so the outer brackets stay literal and the inner link wins. The spec suite passes (1781 tests) and the unit tests pass (44); the standalone type-check and lint were not run because the command was denied, though the esbuild build succeeds. The cause was `outputLink` in `src/Tokenizer.ts`, which lexed the link text and always wrapped the result in a link token. It now checks the lexed text for a link at any nesting depth (including inside emphasis or an image) and, if it finds one, declines to form the outer link. Images are unaffected, since they may contain links. Both examples from the report now give the expected output: - `[foo [bar](/uri)](/uri)` → `

[foo bar](/uri)

` - `[foo [bar](/uri)][ref]` → `

[foo bar]ref

` Two things beyond the core fix: - **Spec flags:** I removed `shouldFail` from examples 518, 519 and 532 in both `test/specs/commonmark/commonmark.0.31.2.json` and `test/specs/gfm/commonmark.0.31.2.json`, since they now pass. - **Deep nesting:** rejected link texts are remembered per lexer, so deeply nested brackets are not re-lexed at every level. 2000 nested links parse in about 4 ms. Example 533 (`[foo *bar [baz][ref]*][ref]`) still fails and remains marked `shouldFail`. The links are now correct, but the `*…*` inside is not rendered as emphasis, because the emphasis masking in `src/Lexer.ts` hides the whole outer reference link. I left that alone as it is a separate issue from the one reported.
